headline: High: ctx can observe Claude Code events while plano has broad network egress, creating default-path leakage and action-conflict risks; prompt-injection risk is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events, so it can ingest another agent’s outputs if wired into the same workflow; plano has broad network egress but no documented shared channel or parser bridge. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default-proven, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF ctx is connected to plano outputs through a shared file, queue, or hook chain, then prompt-injection exposure exists.
IF plano content is copied into ctx-observed Claude Code events, ctx may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or file handoff between the agents.
Require provenance tags on all ctx-observed events.
Insert a manual review step before ctx consumes plano-generated text.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, MCP servers, harness records, graph data, and runtime logs; plano touches logs/metrics/traces and has broad network egress. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive operational data if ctx artifacts are forwarded into plano’s network path, so medium fits the default-risk inference.
conditions: IF ctx writes runtime logs or graph data into a location plano can read, then those data classes can leave the local boundary.
IF plano is configured to forward logs or traces to a remote backend, then ctx-originated content can be exfiltrated.
mitigations: Keep ctx and plano on separate filesystems.
Restrict plano egress to approved destinations only.
Redact logs before any export step.
Rotate or isolate credentials used by either agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and run browsers/install packages, while plano has broad network egress and no subprocesses. Their write surfaces overlap on files and external side effects can race if they share a workspace, but the profiles do not show unrestricted shared git or locking, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, then file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF plano consumes config.yaml while ctx mutates adjacent files, then configuration drift can break runs.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Make shared files read-only for one agent.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Snapshot config.yaml before each run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is explicitly an observer of Claude Code events, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative context by downstream automation; plano is a gateway/proxy with broad network egress, so if it forwards or acts on ctx-derived text without verification, errors can cascade. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF plano forwards ctx-generated text into downstream chat completions or routing decisions without validation, then errors can propagate.
IF ctx emits incorrect facts into logs that plano later reuses, then downstream actions may be based on false premises.
mitigations: Require explicit validation before plano uses ctx output.
Mark ctx output as advisory, not authoritative.
Add a checksum or provenance field to handoffs.
Review one sample handoff per run.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while plano touches logs, metrics, and traces; this creates a retention-policy mismatch risk on operational data, but no residency or regulated-data violation is documented. Only one agent’s compliance surface is directly relevant here, so the other is cited for the shared logging class rather than a specific legal regime.
conditions: IF ctx logs are retained longer than plano traces, then deletion/export requests may be inconsistent.
IF either agent stores personal data in logs, then retention controls must be aligned.
mitigations: Set a common log-retention window.
Purge old traces before sharing data between agents.
Avoid placing personal data in logs.
Document which agent owns deletion requests.
requires-engineering: align retention and subject-rights workflows across both systems.
